title: 2017 AMC 10A Problem 18
statement: Amelia has a coin that lands heads with probability \(\frac{1}{3},\) and Blaine has a coin that lands on heads with probability \(\frac{2}{5}.\) Amelia and Blaine alternately toss their coins until someone gets a head; the first one to get a head wins. All coin tosses are independent. Amelia goes first. The probability that Amelia wins is \(\frac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(q-p?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the probability that Amelia wins.

There is a \(\frac{1}{3}\) chance Amelia wins off her first flip.

If she gets tails, Blaine must also get tails for the game to return to the same state; this happens with probability \(\frac{3}{5}.\)

The total probability of this case is \[\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5}.\]

The game then goes back to Amelia, who then again has a \(x\) chance of winning.

Therefore, we get the following equation. \[ x = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{5}x\]\[\dfrac{3}{5}x = \dfrac{1}{3} \]\[ x = \dfrac{5}{9}. \]

The difference between the denominator and numerator is \(9 - 5 = 4.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let \(x\) be Amelia’s chance to win from the start of her turn
